description: m3 Vina Dock median across 10 pockets (830c, 1h36, 3eml, 3ny8, 4aaw, 4rlu, 1g9v, 2hnx, 4rn0, 1fmc). For each pocket the per-pocket best (most negative) kcal/mol across the 5-candidate x 5-seed sweep is taken; m3 is the median of those 10 per-pocket best values.

r17_reference_baseline_kcal_mol.source: metrics/by_metric/vina_score.json (R17, 830c, 100 Lambda click products, real Vina 1.2.7, exhaustiveness=8)
r17_reference_baseline_kcal_mol.reason: Phase 3 stub scorer differs from R17 real Vina; pocket cohort differs (10 vs 1); candidate pool differs (metal-drugs vs CuAAC click products). R17 reference is shown for context only.

honest_negative.finding: Per-pocket best kcal/mol for se3sb and baseline are identical to floating-point noise (lift_kcal_mol_se3sb_minus_baseline = 1.296312e-08). The stub scorer's deterministic jitter bottom-out at the same -2.0 kcal/mol lower bound for every pocket, so the per-pocket best is the same constant (~-9.6574 kcal/mol) for both methods across all 10 pockets.
honest_negative.implication: No quantitative lift can be claimed from this Phase 3 sweep. The se3sb-vs-baseline lift is consistent with zero (within stub determinism). To measure a real lift we need either (a) the trained W2.1 EGNN velocity field so the SE(3) SB initial pose is biased toward a real sub-pocket, or (b) lower Vina exhaustiveness so the initial pose matters more, plus a meeko extension / non-meeko PDBQT writer that handles Pt/Au/Ru so the real Vina path can run on the metal-drug cohort.
honest_negative.stub_vs_real_vina_organic_cohort: Real Vina on the 5-organic-molecule cohort (CCO/benzene/toluene/TEA/benzamide) returned identical 830c x method kcal/mol means (-3.915) at exhaustiveness=4 (see real_vina_organic/summary.json and notes.md). The SE(3) SB initial pose does not pre-bias Vina at this exhaustiveness, so even a real-Vina sweep at this exhaustiveness would not show lift.

verdict: MEASURED_BUT_STUB — both methods yielded identical per-pocket best to floating-point noise; no quantitative lift. Ship gate (≤ -8.5 kcal/mol) is technically met by both methods because the stub floor is -9.66 kcal/mol, but this is a property of the stub, not of the methods. Reported honestly as a Phase-3 negative.
